parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Sight of correct common denominator $(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)(\sin\theta-\cos\theta)$ and numerator $\sin\theta(\sin\theta-\cos\theta)+\cos\theta(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)$ — *M1; in one or two fractions, condone missing brackets if recovered and $\pm$ sign errors in numerator only.
Obtain $(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta)/(\sin^2\theta-\cos^2\theta)$ and divide throughout by $\cos^2\theta$ — DM1.
$\frac{\tan^2\theta+1}{\tan^2\theta-1}$ AG — A1.
Alternative: replace $\tan^2\theta$ by $\sin^2\theta/\cos^2\theta$ and multiply top and bottom by $\cos^2\theta$ — *M1; sight of convincing partial fractions — DM1; recover the left-hand side — A1 AG.
For working on both sides: M1 DM1 A1 only if both finish at the same correct expression; if started separately, A1 requires a final conclusion such as QED. Do not allow cross multiplication. Condone $s,c,t$ and omission of $\theta$.
Total: 3

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Set $(\tan^2\theta+1)/(\tan^2\theta-1)=2$ and clear the fraction — *M1.
Simplify to $\tan\theta=\pm\sqrt3$ — DM1; may be implied by correct final answer.
Alternative first two marks: equate $(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta)/(\sin^2\theta-\cos^2\theta)$ to 2, clear fraction and use identities to obtain an equation in one function — *M1; simplify to $\sin\theta=\pm\sqrt3/2$ or $\cos\theta=\pm1/2$ — DM1.
$\theta=\pi/3$ — A1; $\theta=2\pi/3$ — A1 FT for $\pi-$ their first value; no others, exact radians. SC B1 for $60^\circ,120^\circ$, or $0.333\pi,0.667\pi$ AWRT, or $1.05,2.09$ AWRT.
Total: 4
